## Source: amazon-inspector (1ba4c643cb0383a3a2631c43deecfb9b0cae27dd209e0117cead1b2e22c3d0c4)
lib/index.js is a webpack bundle whose authored source (per the shipped source map) only re-exports a logger module. An extra line `eval(atob("<~50KB base64>"))` has been appended after the webpack footer and is not present in the authored sources. The decoded blob is heavily obfuscated with an obfuscator.io-style string-array dispatcher (`_0x5c1d` with hex-named helpers and runtime array shuffling) and contains Ethereum JSON-RPC method strings (`eth_blockNumber`, `eth_getBlockByNumber`, `eth_getTransactionCount`), public Ethereum RPC provider hostnames (`*.publicnode.com`, `h.drpc.org`, `public.*.blockscout`), nonce/transaction handling, a browser User-Agent, and `node:http`/`https` POST plumbing. It sets `global.i='A10-npm_inject'` and hooks `module`/`require`/`process`. The payload executes at `require('@adminide-stack/utils')` time, so any consumer importing the package runs the attacker code. The combination of a post-build appended obfuscated loader, mismatch with the authored source map (a utility that only re-exports a logger), and Ethereum RPC interception strings matches the npm wallet-drainer supply-chain campaign and places any wallet/transaction-signing activity reachable from the host process at risk.

## Source: ghsa-malware (ab42798fc40b5b8c35b36e9aab872128a0a06d4f385d2aa56e59bfbf843482f6)
Any computer that has this package installed or running should be considered fully compromised. All secrets and keys stored on that computer should be rotated immediately from a different computer. The package should be removed, but as full control of the computer may have been given to an outside entity, there is no guarantee that removing the package will remove all malicious software resulting from installing it.
